blocks.text: Lots and land in Government Road

items.t: Established-street house lots: freehold detached houses on the residential streets south of Lougheed Highway, with strata townhomes and condos toward the Lougheed and Eastlake side, and industrial and office parcels along the corridor that are outside the residential profile. The corridor mixes houses, strata and industrial/office land — confirm the zone parcel by parcel; the R1 SSMUH unit counts in apply only to R1 lots. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.
Lot character: typical Government Road lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level (no official source read states them).

Bare-land strata: none verified: Stated for the record, because buyers ask: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure — Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply to the lot — but no such lot is documented in Government Road here.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Established lots sit inside that City serviced system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel — and any upgrade a subdivision triggers — is confirmed with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Government Road is confirmed; parcel-level ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Hazard position: Stoney Creek runs through the area to Burnaby Lake and the lake's east shore is low and wet; a floodplain designation for Government Road's residential streets was NOT confirmed in the sources read — parcel-level hazard and watercourse-setback status are property-specific checks, and creek-edge lots need the setback check early.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: none documented as inventory: A specific named residential presale inside the Government Road sub-area confirmed on a City or developer source: Not verified. The Cameron Community Centre and Library replacement (estimated total construction cost $267 million, per the City) is the area's confirmed major civic project — a public facility rebuild, never for-sale land.
Historic subdivisions = built lot fabric, not offerings: the residential streets south of Lougheed Highway are established built fabric; nothing in them is presented as a current lot offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Government Road

items.t: Government Road is the residential and light-industrial corridor in north-east Burnaby running south of Lougheed Highway, between the Lougheed Town Centre / Cameron lands to the east and Burnaby Lake and the Sperling side to the west, named for Government Road and anchored by École Seaforth Elementary at 7881 Government Rd.
Nearby areas: Lougheed Town Centre and Cameron to the east, Cariboo to the south-east, Burnaby Lake to the west and south-west, Montecito and Lochdale to the north across Lougheed Highway.

Main roads and transit: Government Road, Lougheed Highway, Winston Street and Eastlake Drive are the main roads, with Gaglardi Way linking north to SFU. Route 110 is the area's spine bus — from Lougheed Station via Cameron, Beaverbrook, Eastlake, Production Way–University Station, Brighton, Government Road, Phillips and Winston to Sperling Station, then on to Metrotown Station; Government Road itself is on the published route. The Millennium Line stations serving the area are Lougheed Station and Production Way–University Station to the east and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station to the west. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic anchors: Burnaby Lake Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) at the west side — a wildlife sanctuary with a rowing course, rowing pavilion and public canoe launch, Nature House, and viewing towers and docks; the City and Metro Vancouver have signed a 25-year lease for the 360-acre park, which Metro Vancouver has funded and managed since 1978. Stoney Creek Park and Trail System and the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands run through the east side. The Cameron Community Centre and Library replacement is under construction east of the area (old complex closed August 18, 2024; a Temporary Cameron Community Centre and Library operates inside The City of Lougheed Shopping Centre, 110-9855 Austin Avenue). Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12) and catchments are address-based through the SD41 school locator. In-area schools on the Province's list are École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Stoney Creek Community Elementary (K–7), 2740 Beaverbrook Cres, with Cameron Elementary (K–7), 9540 Erickson Dr, and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12), 8800 Eastlake Dr, on the east and north-east side. School names here are Ministry-listed names, spelled exactly.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Government Road

items.t: Subdivision + servicing requirements — base number HELD not confirmed: Burnaby's servicing instrument is the Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw — the former Subdivision Control Bylaw as renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, 2024. The process documented here runs off the zone (new parcels must conform to the Zoning Bylaw for the zone) and the City's servicing-improvements regime for larger residential projects; parcel-level works-and-services requirements are confirmed with the City's Engineering Department for the specific lot before a split is priced.
Watercourse diligence: Stoney Creek and its trail system are dedicated park lands and the setback rules travel with the creek — check watercourse setbacks early on creek-edge lots.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Government Road ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Government Road

items.t: The original Seaforth School dates to 1922 — and it is not on Government Road anymore: the City's heritage record dates the original Seaforth School to 1922, since relocated to Burnaby Village Museum — the corridor's dated anchor is a moved heritage schoolhouse, while the current École Seaforth Elementary stands at 7881 Government Rd.

Burnaby Lake's park status was re-signed for 25 years (February 5, 2025): the City and Metro Vancouver signed a 25-year lease for Burnaby Lake Regional Park, which Metro Vancouver has funded and managed since 1978, covering the 360-acre park at Government Road's west side — west-edge lots back onto a secured regional park, not onto land awaiting a plan.
Stoney Creek Park carries 2 tennis and 2 pickleball courts on the City's outdoor courts list — a small, checkable amenity fact for the creek-side streets that most corridor marketing never mentions.

Burnaby replaced its entire zoning bylaw effective July 1, 2026: the Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026) repealed the 1965 bylaw (No. 4742) — any older guide or disclosure citing the 1965 zoning bylaw for a Government Road lot is out of date.

faq.a: No verified one — the corridor is established houses, strata pockets and industrial/office land; no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering was verified.
faq.q: Is there a vacant-lot subdivision or a lot presale I can buy into on Government Road?

faq.a: If the lot is R1, yes — under Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District a house lot may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and multi-unit lots may be stratified. Corridor parcels in other zones follow their own zone, so confirm the parcel's zone first.
faq.q: Can a Government Road house lot add units?

faq.a: Both exist on this corridor: houses and strata sit south of Lougheed Highway, and the Lake City industrial and office lands run along the Lougheed corridor as the area's employment side. A corridor parcel's zone is confirmed parcel by parcel — never assume R1.
faq.q: Is the lot I am looking at residential or industrial land?

faq.a: Stoney Creek Park and Trail System and the conservation lands are dedicated park lands running through the area's east side toward Burnaby Lake, and the setback rules travel with the creek — check watercourse setbacks early, and note no floodplain designation for the residential streets was confirmed.
faq.q: Does the Stoney Creek edge affect a lot?

faq.a: The City's utility wording puts established homes on annual water and sewer billing (detached water charge $652.33 for 2026, a 5% discount if paid by the due date, sewer as a parcel tax for single-family homes) — confirm the specific parcel's connections and any servicing upgrade a subdivision will require.
faq.q: Is a Government Road lot serviced?

faq.a: In north-east Burnaby, south of Lougheed Highway between Lougheed Town Centre and Burnaby Lake, named for Government Road and anchored by École Seaforth Elementary at 7881 Government Rd; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area within the City of Burnaby.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Government Road address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Stoney Creek Community Elementary (K–7), 2740 Beaverbrook Cres, with Cameron Elementary and Burnaby Mountain Secondary on the east side; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: How is transit on Government Road?
faq.a: Route 110 runs on Government Road itself, linking Lougheed Station and Production Way–University Station to the east with Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station and Metrotown Station to the west, via Beaverbrook, Eastlake, Brighton, Phillips and Winston.
